item.title: - What do you think, headman? If your son Ciravāsi were to be killed, captured, harmed, or criticized, would you experience sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief,…
item.description:
- What do you think, headman? If your son Ciravāsi were to be killed, captured, harmed, or criticized, would you experience sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair?" - "Venerable Sir, if my son Ciravāsi were to be killed, captured, harmed, criticized, or his life were to change, how could I not experience sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair?" - "By this method, headman, it should be understood: Whatever suffering arises, all of it has desire as its root, desire as its cause. Desire is the root of suffering.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 42.11

item.title: - Venerable Girimānanda, Venerable Sir, is sick, suffering, gravely ill. It would be good, Venerable Sir, if the Blessed One would visit Venerable Girimānanda out…
item.description:
- Venerable Girimānanda, Venerable Sir, is sick, suffering, gravely ill. It would be good, Venerable Sir, if the Blessed One would visit Venerable Girimānanda out of compassion.
- Ānanda, if you go to the bhikkhu Girimānanda and recite ten perceptions, then this is possible: after hearing the ten perceptions, the bhikkhu Girimānanda's illness may immediately subside! What ten? The perception of impermanence, the perception of non-self, the perception of foulness, the perception of danger, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence in all conditioned things, and mindfulness of breathing.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.60

item.title: Of little value, bhikkhus, are these kinds of growth, such as growth in wealth. This is the foremost among kinds of growth, bhikkhus, namely growth…
item.description:
Of little value, bhikkhus, are these kinds of growth, such as growth in wealth. This is the foremost among kinds of growth, bhikkhus, namely growth in wisdom. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: 'We will achieve growth in wisdom.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.79

item.title: Bhikkhus, whatever in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, among the multitude of ascetics and brahmins, devas and humans, is seen ... examined…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, whatever in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, among the multitude of ascetics and brahmins, devas and humans, is seen ... examined by the mind — all that I know. Bhikkhus, whatever in this world ... is seen ... examined by the mind — I have directly known it thus: 'All that the Tathāgata has known. The Tathāgata does not hold to it.' Bhikkhus, if I were to say: 'I know all that in this world ... is seen ... examined by the mind' — that would be false speech in me. If I were to say: 'I both know and do not know' — that would be false speech in me. If I were to say: 'I neither know nor do not know' — that would be false speech in me. Thus there would be an error in me.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.24

item.title: Kassapa, one speaking rightly would say: 'One living the holy life must endure the hardships of the holy life. One living the holy life must…
item.description:
Kassapa, one speaking rightly would say: 'One living the holy life must endure the hardships of the holy life. One living the holy life must be oppressed by the pressures of the holy life.' Speaking thus, Kassapa, one speaks rightly. One living the holy life must endure the hardships of the holy life. One living the holy life must be oppressed by the pressures of the holy life.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 16.8
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Bhikkhus, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye, seeing beings with little dust in their eyes,…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye, seeing beings with little dust in their eyes, with much dust in their eyes, with keen faculties, with dull faculties, with good qualities, with bad qualities, easy to teach, hard to teach, and some who saw the danger in future rebirth and the danger in faulty actions. Just as in a pond of blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses, some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, do not rise above the water, thrive while submerged; some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, live reaching the water's surface; some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, rise above the water and stand without being wetted by the water.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 14 – Mahāpadānasutta

item.title: - Just as, bhikkhus, those families that have many women and few men are easily harassed by thieves and robbers. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu…
item.description:
- Just as, bhikkhus, those families that have many women and few men are easily harassed by thieves and robbers. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who does not develop and cultivate the liberation of mind by loving-kindness is easily harassed by non-humans. - Just as, bhikkhus, those families that have few women and many men are not easily harassed by thieves and robbers. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the liberation of mind by loving-kindness is not easily harassed by non-humans. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: 'We will develop the liberation of mind by loving-kindness, cultivate it, make it our vehicle, make it our base, establish it, accumulate it, and properly undertake it.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 20.3

item.title: Elder Nun Soṇā: I gave birth to ten children From this accumulative body. Therefore I was weak and aged. I went to a bhikkhunī. She…
item.description:
Elder Nun Soṇā:

I gave birth to ten children
From this accumulative body.
Therefore I was weak and aged.
I went to a bhikkhunī.

She taught me the Dhamma,
About aggregates, sense spheres, and elements.
Hearing the Dhamma she taught,
I shaved my hair and went forth.

I followed her instruction.
My divine eye was purified,
I know my past lives,
Where I lived before.

I developed the signless Dhamma,
One-pointed, well concentrated.
Instantly I was liberated,
Without clinging, at peace.

The five aggregates are fully understood,
They stand with roots cut off.
I have no sensual desire,
No firm foundation.
From now on, there is no
Issue of renewed existence.

From: Therīgāthā 5.8

item.title: Elder Nun Sumānā: O that elder nun, Lie down happily, Covered in your robe, Made by yourself. Your greed is calmed, You are cooled, at…
item.description:
Elder Nun Sumānā:

O that elder nun,
Lie down happily,
Covered in your robe,
Made by yourself.
Your greed is calmed,
You are cooled, at peace.

From: Therīgāthā 1.16

item.title: When you gather together, bhikkhus, there are two things to be done: discussing the Dhamma or maintaining noble silence." Then the Blessed One, having understood…
item.description:
When you gather together, bhikkhus, there are two things to be done: discussing the Dhamma or maintaining noble silence." Then the Blessed One, having understood the meaning of this, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

One who lives without worldly work,
Light, desiring welfare,
With faculties restrained,
Fully liberated,

Homeless, without 'I-making',
Without sensual desire, having slain Māra,
Such a bhikkhu
Lives alone.

From: Udāna 3.9
